query: What nationality were social anthropologists Alfred Gell and Edmund Leach?

pipeline_result.response: Social anthropologists Alfred Gell and Edmund Leach were British social anthropologists who studied art, language, symbolism, and ritual. They both had degrees in anthropology from the London School of Economics and trained under Edmund Leach's guidance. Edmund Leach was a Fellow of the British Academy, while Alfred Gell taught at the London School of Economics.
retrieved_context: Alfred Gell: Alfred Antony Francis Gell, {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} ( ; June 12, 1945 – January 28, 1997) was a British social anthropologist whose most influential work concerned art, language, symbolism and ritual.  He was trained by Edmund Leach (MPhil, Cambridge University) and Raymond Firth (PhD, London School of Economics) and did his fieldwork in Melanesia and tribal India.  Gell taught at the London School of Economics, among other places.  He was also a Fellow of the British Academy.  He died of cancer in 1997, at the age of 51.
Edmund Leach: Sir Edmund Ronald Leach (7 November 1910 – 6 January 1989) was a British social anthropologist.
Edmund the Martyr: Edmund the Martyr (also known as St Edmund or Edmund of East Anglia, died 20 November 869) was king of East Anglia from about 855 until his death.
